skills.name: Proportions in figures
skills.wrong_turn: Keep the same order on both sides: small/big = small/big. Flipping just one ratio, like 4/6 = 15/10, gives a wrong answer.

skills.name: Similar polygons
skills.wrong_turn: Not all rectangles are similar. A 2 × 3 and a 3 × 4 rectangle have equal angles, but 3/2 ≠ 4/3.
skills.rule: Similar polygons have all matching angles equal and all matching sides in the same ratio.

skills.name: Scale factor
skills.wrong_turn: Scale factor is new over original. Shrinking 10 cm to 4 cm is k = 0.4, not 2.5.
skills.rule: k=(new lengthoriginal length); k>1 enlarges, k<1 reduces.

skills.name: AA similarity
skills.wrong_turn: Match the equal angles when you name the triangles. If ∠A = ∠Q and ∠B = ∠P, write △ABC ∼ △QPR, not △PQR.
skills.rule: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the triangles are similar.

skills.name: SSS similarity
skills.wrong_turn: Sort the sides by size before comparing. 4, 6, 8 and 12, 9, 6 are similar, but 4/12 ≠ 6/9 in the order written.

skills.name: SAS similarity

steps.a: two ratios and the included angle

skills.wrong_turn: The angle must be between the two sides. Two proportional sides and a non-included angle do not prove similarity.
skills.rule: If two sides are proportional and the angles between them are equal, the triangles are similar.

skills.name: Triangle proportionality
skills.wrong_turn: Don't mix pieces with wholes: AD/DB = AE/EC, but DE/BC equals AD/AB, not AD/DB.
skills.rule: If DE∥BC with D on AB and E on AC, then (ADDB)=(AEEC).

skills.name: Angle bisector theorem
skills.wrong_turn: The angle bisector does not cut the opposite side in half; that's the median. It splits it in the ratio of the other two sides.
skills.rule: The bisector of ∠A meets BC at D with (BDDC)=(ABAC).

skills.name: Similar right triangles
skills.wrong_turn: The altitude is the geometric mean of the two hypotenuse pieces, not their average. Pieces 4 and 9 give 6, not 6.5.
skills.rule: The altitude to the hypotenuse gives h2=pq, a2=pc and b2=qc.

skills.name: Perimeter & area ratios
skills.wrong_turn: Doubling the sides doesn't double the area. It multiplies the area by 4.
skills.rule: With scale factor k, perimeters multiply by k and areas by k2.

skills.name: Volume ratios
skills.wrong_turn: Doubling a solid's size doesn't double its volume. It multiplies volume by 8 and surface area by 4.
skills.rule: With scale factor k, surface areas multiply by k2 and volumes by k3.

skills.name: Indirect measurement
skills.wrong_turn: Keep matching things in matching places: height/shadow = height/shadow. Writing 1.8/40 = h/2.4 gives a tower 0.1 m tall.
skills.rule: Build similar triangles you can measure, then scale up.
